title: Risotto ai Funghi
subtitle: Classic mushroom risotto
excerpt: A creamy, deeply savoury mushroom risotto built on the slow addition of hot stock and finished with a generous amount of butter and parmesan. The technique is simple but requires attention; risotto rewards patience at the hob.
sourceNotes: Risotto ai funghi is a pillar of northern Italian cooking, particularly from Lombardy and the Veneto. The method of slowly incorporating hot stock while stirring to release the starch from arborio rice was perfected in the Po Valley, where rice has been cultivated since the fifteenth century.

content.text: Keep the stock hot in a separate small pan throughout cooking. Adding cold stock drops the temperature of the risotto and slows the cooking, leading to an uneven texture. The risotto is done when it flows slowly across the plate when you tilt it, known in Italian as all'onda, meaning wave-like.

items.prepNote: kept hot in a separate pan

content.text: Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over a high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes until they are golden and have released their liquid. Add the garlic and thyme, cook for 1 more minute, then transfer the mushrooms to a bowl and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and add half the butter to the pan. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the arborio rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are coated and starting to turn translucent at the edges.

Add a ladleful of hot stock and stir constantly until it has been absorbed. Continue adding stock one ladleful at a time, waiting until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18 to 20 minutes.
When the rice is cooked but still has a little bite, stir in the reserved mushrooms. Remove from the heat and beat in the remaining cold butter and the parmesan. The risotto should flow like lava.
Leave to rest for 2 minutes, then serve immediately in warmed bowls scattered with parsley.

items.cause: Too much stock was added at once, or it was stirred too infrequently.
items.fix: Add stock one ladle at a time and stir steadily throughout.

items.cause: The risotto was underdone; not enough stock was used.
items.fix: Add more hot stock and cook for 3 to 4 more minutes.

items.symptom: Mushrooms are steaming and grey rather than golden.
items.cause: The pan was overcrowded or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cook mushrooms in a single layer over high heat without stirring.
